operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts William C. Alden from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending September 30, 1942". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1942-09-30 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1942-09-30 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1942-10-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that William C. Alden, Principal Scientist (Geologist), Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 401 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said William C. Alden from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Wladimir Ayvazoglou, senior translator, Geological Survey, Department of the Interior, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Wladimir Ayvazoglou from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Dr. Arthur R. Butler from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending March 31, 1943". operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Dr. Arthur R. Butler, senior medical officer, United States Civil Service Commission, who, during the month of March, 1942, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Dr. Arthur R. Butler from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending March 31, 1943.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Burt W. Andrews from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending November 30, 1942". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1942-11-30 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1942-11-30 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1942-12-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Burt W. Andrews, principal attorney, Bureau of Internal Revenue, Treasury Department, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Burt W. Andrews from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending November 30, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Clause 1 establishes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area and prescribes its control regulations. EO 9720, signed by President Truman on May 8, 1946, states that the listed areas "are hereby discontinued" and lists the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by Executive Order No. 8953 of November 27, 1941, as item 5. EO 9720 is an express discontinuance of the area by a later order that names it and whose text is held. The regulations, the call for assistance and the Navy charge are tied by their own words to this area, so they ended with it. EO 9720 states no separate effective date; the signing date is recorded, and the Federal Register publication date was May 10, 1946.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by the provisions of
section 44 of the Criminal Code, as
amended (U.S.C., title 18, sec. 96), the
following-described area is hereby estab­
lished for purposes of national defense
as a defensive sea area, to be known as
the “Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor
Naval Defensive Sea Area”:
All United States territorial waters ol Los
Angeles-Long Beach Harbor and Its ap­
proaches and tributaries from the contour
line of extreme high water on the shores of
these waters, as shown on the latest US.C.
and G.S. charts, to the following seaward
limits:
A line running along bearing 160° true
from Whites Point, California, in approxi­
mate Latitude 33° 42' 51” North, Longitude
118° 19' West, to the seaward limit of United
States territorial waters;
A line running along bearing 210° true
from a point on the shore of Huntington
Beach, California, in Latitude 33° 39' 47”
North, Longitude 118° 00' 41” West, to the
seaward limit of United States territorial
waters; and
A line running along the seaward limit of
United States territorial waters between the
above-described bearing lines.
A vessel not proceeding under United
States naval or other United States au­
thorized supervision shall not enter or
navigate the waters of the Los Angeles-
Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea
Area except during daylight, when good
visibility conditions prevail, and then
only after specific permission has been
obtained. Advance arrangements for
entry into or navigation through or
within the Los Angeles-Long Beach Har­
bor Naval Defensive Sea Area must be
made, preferably by application to a
United States Naval District Headquar­
ters in advance of sailing, or by radio or
visual communication on approaching
the seaward limits of the area. If radio
telegraphy is used, the call “NQO” shall
be made on a frequency of 500 Kcs and
permission to enter the port requested.
The name of the vessel, purpose of entry,
and name of the master must be given
in the request. If visual communica­
tions are used, the procedure shall be
essentially the same.
A v e s s e l e n t er i n g o r n a v i g at i n g th e
wa te r s o f th e L o s A n g e l es - L o n g B ea ch
Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area does
so at its own risk.
Even though permission has been ob­
tained, it is incumbent upon a vessel en­
tering the Los Angeles-Long Beach Har­
bor Naval Defensive Sea Area to obey any
further instructions received from the
United States Navy or other United
States authority.
A vessel may expect supervision of its
movements within the Los Angeles-Long
Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area,
either through surface craft or aircraft.
Such controlling surface craft and air­
craft shall be identified by a prominent
display of the Union Jack.
The loading or unloading by vessels of
oil fuel or other inflammable or explosive
materials shall be under the control of
the local naval authority, who shall re­
quire such loading or unloading to be ac­
complished in such manner and at such
times as will safeguard the other activi­
ties within the Los Angeles-Long Beach
Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area essen­
tial to the national defense.
These regulations are subject to am­
plification by the local United States
naval authority as necessary to meet local
circumstances and conditions.
When a United States Maritime Con­
trol Area is established adjacent to or
abutting upon the Los Angeles-Long
Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area,
it shall be assumed that permission to
enter, and other instructions issued by
proper authority, shall apply to any one
continuous passage through or within
both areas.
Any master of a vessel or other person
within the Los Angeles-Long Beach Har­
bor Naval Defensive Sea Area who shall
disregard these regulations, or shall fail
to obey an order of United States naval
authority to stop or heave-to, or shall
perform any act threatening the effi­
ciency of mines or other defenses or the
safety of navigation, or shall take any
action inimical to the interest of the
United States, may be detained therein
by force of arms and renders himself
liable to attack by the armed forces of
the United States, and liable to prose­
cution as provided for in section 44 of
the Criminal Code, as amended (U.S.C.,
title 18, sec. 96).
All United States Government authori­
ties shall place at the disposal of the
naval authorities their facilities for aid­
ing in the enforcement of these regula­
tions. Tile Governor of the State of
California, the local municipal officials,
and the local civilian defense agencies
are called upon to render the local naval
authorities all possible assistance in the
enforcement of these regulations.
The Secretary of the Navy shall be
charged with the publication and en­
forcement of these regulations.

Naval Defensive Sea Area”:
All United States territorial waters ol Los
Angeles-Long Beach Harbor and Its ap­
proaches and tributaries from the contour
line of extreme high water on the shores of
these waters, as shown on the latest US.C.
and G.S. charts, to the following seaward
limits:
A line running along bearing 160° true
from Whites Point, California, in approxi­
mate Latitude 33° 42' 51” North, Longitude
118° 19' West, to the seaward limit of United
States territorial waters;
A line running along bearing 210° true
from a point on the shore of Huntington
Beach, California, in Latitude 33° 39' 47”
North, Longitude 118° 00' 41” West, to the
seaward limit of United States territorial
waters; and
A line running along the seaward limit of
United States territorial waters between the
above-described bearing lines.

States naval or other United States au­
thorized supervision shall not enter or
navigate the waters of the Los Angeles-
Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea

visibility conditions prevail, and then
only after specific permission has been
obtained. Advance arrangements for
entry into or navigation through or
within the Los Angeles-Long Beach Har­
bor Naval Defensive Sea Area must be
made, preferably by application to a
United States Naval District Headquar­
ters in advance of sailing, or by radio or
visual communication on approaching
the seaward limits of the area. If radio
telegraphy is used, the call “NQO” shall
be made on a frequency of 500 Kcs and

and name of the master must be given
in the request. If visual communica­

charged with the publication and en­
forcement of these regulations.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Clause 2 states that the order supersedes Executive Order No. 8403 of May 7, 1940, which had established the same area. A supersession sentence is performed when the order issues, so the command was exhausted on the order's date, November 27, 1941; the order states no later effective date. Its result, that EO 8403 no longer operated, is an accrued effect that is not undone by the later discontinuance of the area.

research_rationale:
The registered working text is the Federal Register text layer of EO 8953 (6 FR 6123, Federal Register of December 2, 1941; machine-extracted text, original page images not inspected). The order is dated November 27, 1941 and establishes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area under section 44 of the Criminal Code, prescribes the regulations for vessels in it, calls on Government and local authorities to assist in enforcing them, charges the Secretary of the Navy with their publication and enforcement, and supersedes Executive Order No. 8403 of May 7, 1940. Inventory corrected into two clauses: the area and its regulations (characters 714 to 5507 of the held text) and the one-time supersession sentence (characters 5508 to 5666). Clause 1 ends by express discontinuance in EO 9720 of May 8, 1946 (11 FR 5105, Federal Register of May 10, 1946; filed May 9, 1946), whose list of areas discontinued includes the Los Angeles-Long Beach Harbor Naval Defensive Sea Area established by Executive Order No. 8953 of November 27, 1941. Clause 2 was performed when the order issued on November 27, 1941. Recorded date for the end of clause 1 is the signing date, May 8, 1946, because EO 9720 states no other effective date; publication in the Federal Register was May 10, 1946. Provisional text: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Nicholas W. Dorsey from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1943-01-31 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1943-01-31 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1943-02-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Nicholas W. Dorsey, accountant and auditor, Smithsonian Institution, who, during the month of January, 1942, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Nicholas W. Dorsey from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole command revokes, by the words of the order, all Executive orders or parts thereof establishing airspace reservations within the continental limits of the United States except the District of Columbia, and the order does not apply to Alaska or the Panama Canal Zone. The command operated when the order issued on December 6, 1941 and was thereby exhausted; its result, the revocation, survives as an accrued effect. EO 10768 of May 16, 1958 recites that EO 7138 was revoked as to its other airspace reservations by this order, which shows the revocation took effect, but it does not revoke or amend this order and is a later event, not an end. The order states no effective date other than its date; filing in the Federal Register was December 9, 1941.

research_rationale:
The registered working text is the Federal Register text layer of EO 8961 (6 FR 6325, Federal Register of December 10, 1941; machine-extracted, original page images not inspected). The order is dated December 6, 1941 and contains one command: that all Executive orders or parts thereof establishing airspace reservations within the continental limits of the United States, except the District of Columbia, are revoked, with a closing sentence that it does not apply to Alaska or to the Panama Canal Zone. The command revokes by its own words and was performed when the order issued, so it was exhausted on December 6, 1941. A revocation order's command is spent on performance; its result, the revocation of the reached orders, is the surviving effect. Evidence that the revocation operated: EO 10768 of May 16, 1958 states that Executive Order No. 7138 was revoked as to its other airspace reservations by this order. EO 10768 recites this order and revokes EO 7138; it does not revoke or amend EO 8961 and is recorded as a later event, not an end. The Federal Register filing date was December 9, 1941 and publication December 10, 1941; the signing date is recorded because the order states no other effective date. Provisional text: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Bart W. Butler from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1942-12-31 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1942-12-31 begins, is the alternative. operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Bart W. Butler, Chief of the General Section of the Criminal Division, Department of Justice, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Bart W. Butler from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Mrs. Ethel A. Barnes from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1942-12-31 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1942-12-31 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1943-01-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Mrs. Ethel A. Barnes, chief file clerk, American Embassy, Mexico City, Mexico, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to her, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Mrs. Ethel A. Barnes from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts Miss Roberta L. Lindsey from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1942-12-31 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1942-12-31 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1943-01-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Miss Roberta L. Lindsey, administrative officer, Division of Loans and Currency, Bureau of the Public Debt, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 8610 of December 11, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat, 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, section 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Miss Roberta L. Lindsey from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that all employees in the field service of the Post Office Department who, during the month of December 1941, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, by reason of their becoming either 62 or 65 years of age, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Frank Burke, agent, Secret Service Division, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8302 of December 12, 1939, and No. 8584 of November 7, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Frank Burke from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1942.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

source.quote: Mays from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sole operative clause: the order exempts John W. Mays from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943". This is the order's own stated expiry, not a report deadline and not an amendment. The end is recorded inclusive as 1943-01-31 (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption ends when 1943-01-31 begins, is the alternative. On the inclusive reading the first day without the exemption is 1943-02-01. Actor: the order itself (President Franklin D. Roosevelt). Mechanism: expiry of the order's own fixed term. No later event amends or extends this order in the held record.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that John W. Mays, messenger, The White House Office, Executive Office of the President, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said John W. Mays from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

research_rationale:
The held text of EO 9010 (registered working text: American Presidency Project mirror transcription, not an official edition; original not yet held) is a short order dated 1942-01-03. Its only operative sentence exempts John W. Mays from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, for a period of one year, ending 1943-01-31. The order states its own term and contains no renewal, conditional, revocation or successor provision, so the exemption ends on its own terms. Evidence: the stated term "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1943" is the first end. Recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of 1943-01-31); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when 1943-01-31 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until-dates).
